## Headline lifespan figures (standard lab conditions, from each review's "Headline" section)
| Organism | Median lifespan |
|---|---|
| C. elegans | 18 days |
| D. melanogaster | 60 days |
| S. cerevisiae | 25 divisions (replicative, not calendar time) |
| N. furzeri (killifish) | 16 weeks |
| M. musculus (mouse) | 30 months |
| D. rerio (zebrafish) | 42 months |

Ordered shortest to longest in calendar time: C. elegans (18 d) < fly (60 d) < killifish (16 wk, about 112 d) < mouse (30 mo) < zebrafish (42 mo). Yeast is measured in divisions, so it can't be placed on this axis directly.

## Discussion-section data (per-cohort entries)
I have not reproduced every per-cohort number here.
- Each review has several hundred entries (I did not count them exactly). All use the same template: "In cohort X-NN, median survival of <organism> was P% of controls (n=…, <intervention>, lab …)".
- Across all six organisms:
  - Relative median survival ranges from about 40% to 160% of controls.
  - n ranges from about 20 to 400.
  - Labs are numbered 1–40.
  - Interventions are dietary restriction, rapamycin, metformin, heat stress and daf-2 RNAi.
- Cohort IDs repeat within a file with different values. Examples are C. elegans H-59 (137%, n=235, dietary restriction, lab 17, and also 47%, n=103, rapamycin, lab 16) and C. elegans F-91 (156% and 149%).
- Results look essentially random and wide-ranging, with no obvious intervention-specific pattern. The same interventions are applied to every organism, including daf-2 RNAi in yeast and in flies, which is biologically odd.
- I have not computed means or medians per organism or per intervention. These entries are noisy and probably not reliable for ranking organisms. If needed, I can re-read a file and aggregate it.
- None of the reviews gives explicit throughput data such as cohort size per run, cost, or time-to-result. Any throughput comparison has to be inferred from the lifespan scale (shorter lifespan means faster experiments) and from the n values. I should state that limitation in the synthesis.
